heading_en: Taking Liquidity Horizons into Account in Calculating Expected Shortfall
summary_ja: 流動性ホライズンを勘案した期待ショート・フォールの算式、流動性ホライズンの区分、リスク・クラス別の期間（表）、及びより長い期間の承認申請要件を定める。
summary_en: Sets the expected shortfall formula that takes liquidity horizons into account, the liquidity horizon categories, the periods by risk class and risk factor category (table), and the conditions for applying for approval of longer periods.
paragraphs: An Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the internal model approach shall calculate expected shortfall daily, for the trading desks using the internal model approach as a whole and for portfolios on a per-trading-desk basis, using the following formula. In this case, a one-tailed 97.5 percent confidence level and a liquidity horizon of 10 days (hereinafter in this paragraph referred to as the "base horizon") shall be used in the formula. {{F:p339i0}} ES is the market risk equivalent amount calculated by expected shortfall; ES_{T}(P) is the market risk equivalent amount calculated by expected shortfall for shocks to all risk factors of position P = (p_{i}) on the assumption of the base horizon; T is the length of the base horizon; LH_{j} is the period provided for in the following paragraph; ES_{T}(P, j) is the market risk equivalent amount calculated by expected shortfall that takes into account shocks to each position p_{i} in the set Q(p_{i}, j) of risk factors of position P = (p_{i}) (meaning shocks to each position p_{i} where risk factors whose liquidity horizon n provided for in paragraph (3) is equal to or longer than LH_{j} are varied).

LH_{j} in the preceding paragraph shall be the period set out in the lower column of the following table according to the liquidity horizon category set out in the upper column of that table. {{T:p339t0}}

The liquidity horizon n shall be the period set out in the lower column of the following table according to the risk class set out in the upper column and the risk factor category set out in the middle column of that table; provided, however, that where an Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the internal model approach has obtained the approval of the Commissioner of the Financial Services Agency, it may set a period longer than that period. In this case, the longer period shall be 20 days, 40 days, 60 days or 120 days. {{T:p340t0}} (Note 1) Specified currencies means the currency of the participating countries of the European Economic and Monetary Union (EUR), the currency of the United States of America (USD), the currency of the United Kingdom (GBP), the currency of Australia (AUD), the currency of Sweden (SEK), the currency of Canada (CAD) and the currency of Japan (the same applies in Article 263-2, paragraph (4)). (Note 2) Specified currency pairs means currency pairs consisting of a combination of two currencies among the specified currencies, the currency of Switzerland (CHF), the currency of Mexico (MXN), the currency of the People's Republic of China (CNY), the currency of New Zealand (NZD), the currency of Russia (RUB), the currency of the People's Republic of China (Hong Kong Special Administrative Region) (HKD), the currency of Singapore (SGD), the currency of Turkey (TRY), the currency of the Republic of Korea (KRW), the currency of the Republic of South Africa (ZAR), the currency of India (INR), the currency of Norway (NOK) and the currency of Brazil (BRL).

An Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the internal model approach seeking the approval under the proviso to the preceding paragraph shall submit to the Commissioner of the Financial Services Agency an application for approval attaching documents showing that it conforms to all of the following requirements. (i) Establishing a framework capable of submitting information on the liquidity horizon for each risk factor category upon request of the Commissioner of the Financial Services Agency; (ii) Formulating a policy on the setting of liquidity horizons; (iii) Establishing a framework for regularly conducting verification by the risk management function and internal audit concerning the setting of liquidity horizons.
